definitions.explanation: Successfully maintaining or achieving two things at the same time, especially when they seem difficult to combine. Commonly used for work-life balance, studies and hobbies, career and family.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}と{育児|いくじ}を{両立|りょうりつ}させる。
{勉強|べんきょう}と{部活|ぶかつ}の{両立|りょうりつ}は{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Balancing studies and club activities is tough.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}{成長|せいちょう}と{環境|かんきょう}{保護|ほご}の{両立|りょうりつ}は{現代|げんだい}{社会|しゃかい}の{大|おお}きな{課題|かだい}だ。
examples.english: Balancing economic growth and environmental protection is a major challenge for modern society.

notes:
{両立|りょうりつ} implies successfully managing two things that are typically hard to combine.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- AとBを{両立|りょうりつ}させる (balance A and B)
- AとBの{両立|りょうりつ} (the coexistence of A and B)
- {両立|りょうりつ}が{難|むずか}しい (hard to balance both)
- {両立|りょうりつ}できる (can balance both)

FREQUENT PAIRS:
- {仕事|しごと}と{家庭|かてい} (work and family)
- {仕事|しごと}と{育児|いくじ} (work and child-rearing)
- {勉強|べんきょう}と{部活|ぶかつ} (studies and club activities)
- {経済|けいざい}と{環境|かんきょう} (economy and environment)
